breaking_changes.BC_description: The onFID() function has been removed as it was deprecated. This includes the removal of onFID from the main and attribution exports, FIDThresholds, FIDMetric and related types, and all associated code. This will break any code that still uses this function or its related exports. The removal is part of the v5 branch update, as referenced in the pull request and commit messages.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Replace calls to onFID() with onINP() as the recommended alternative for measuring input responsiveness, since FID is deprecated and INP is its successor. Example: Instead of `onFID(callback)`, use `onINP(callback)`.

breaking_changes.BC_description: The browser support policy has been changed to Baseline Widely available, which may affect compatibility with older browsers not meeting this baseline.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Ensure that the target browsers for your project meet the Baseline Widely available criteria. Update browser lists or configurations accordingly.
breaking_changes.RequireInfo: The specific criteria for 'Baseline Widely available' are not defined. Please clarify what browsers or versions are included and any necessary configuration changes.

breaking_changes.BC_description: The getSelector function in attribution-related modules now sorts class names alphabetically in the generated selector string to reduce cardinality. This changes the order of class names in selectors, which may affect downstream code that relies on a specific order for matching or other purposes.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Review and update any code that depends on the specific order of class names in selectors generated by getSelector. For example, if you previously expected a non-sorted order, ensure your code does not hardcode the order. Instead, use the selector as provided or implement custom sorting if necessary. Code example: Before: const selector = getSelector(element); // Might have classes in original order. After: const selector = getSelector(element); // Classes are now sorted alphabetically; adjust any logic that assumed a different order.
